qa_audit.ip_note: Fictional. "OVERDRIVE" is a generic English dictionary word used as an invented scholarship-merch brand persona (grounded in an Upwork-style brief); not tied to or confusingly close to a specific real trademark. Only allowed real names appear as channels (social PFPs, hoodies) and the Adobe platform.
qa_audit.doable_note: All 14 steps are real connector actions with no banned capability. Fills are SOLID-color only (#000/#FFF/navy tint), bg-removal/crop/select/vectorize/mono-tint/font_recommend/firefly_board all allowed; step 14 is the one permitted local zip. Spec explicitly excludes from-scratch logo gen, AI object removal, compositing, and upscaling. Caveat: step 11 builds a multi-swatch palette via a single image_fill_area call — still solid-fill (not banned gen-fill) but over-claimed, since one fill_area is one selection + one color; realistically needs a built canvas with select + multiple fills.
qa_audit.presentation_note: Complete and well-formed: one deliverable set, clear full_brief, inputs with realism_notes, outputs with specs, coherent output→input chain, reverify present, honest scoping note. Two minor weaknesses (both already caught in reverify): (1) step 13 create_firefly_board consumes overdrive_hoodie_mock.jpg as a tile, but that raw input is never uploaded via a connector step (only the logo lockup is uploaded in steps 1-2) — the board consumes asset URNs, so the hoodie needs its own upload step; (2) step 11 palette-swatch fill is loosely specified/over-claimed as one fill_area call.
qa_audit.top_issue: Chaining gap: the hoodie mock is added to the Firefly usage board (step 13) but is never uploaded via a connector step, so it has no referenceable asset URN — needs an explicit upload step. Also step 11's multi-swatch palette in a single fill_area is over-claimed. Both minor/fixable; no IP, banned-capability, or doability failure.
